title: Tenant onboarding request prioritization ladder — RBAC/SSO/SCIM
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Many enterprise customers submit ad-hoc admin and access requests during onboarding: RBAC templates, SSO/SAML mappings, SCIM delta provisioning, org-policy exceptions (IP allowlists, data residency toggles). Current intake channels (support tickets + email) lack consistent priority signals and routing, causing slow turnarounds and operational overhead for PM/Eng/Solutions.

Goal:
Design and pilot a 'prioritization ladder' for tenant onboarding/admin requests that: 1) classifies requests by risk/complexity/customer-value, 2) produces an actionable priority score for routing, 3) outputs the canonical work item metadata consumed by engineering and solutions (SLA, required artifacts, target owner), and 4) reduces average triage-to-ack time from ~72h to <24h for high-impact enterprise requests.

Scope (non-bug):
- RBAC template requests (new roles, custom role approvals)
- SSO/SAML mapping adjustments and metadata ingestion
- SCIM provisioning delta handling (group mappings, attribute transforms)
- Org policy exceptions (temporary allowlists, delegated admin scopes)
- Excludes security incident handling, post-production incident remediation, or infra-only capacity requests

Proposal & Prioritization Ladder (heuristic):
Tier 0 (Immediate, SLA 4h): security-blocking onboarding items (SSO failing for entire org, SCIM causing account lockouts), legal/regulatory holds (data sovereignty enforcement), customer at Enterprise Contract with live revenue blocking.
Tier 1 (High, SLA 24h): RBAC changes that unlock product features for paid teams, SAML metadata errors affecting >10 users, SCIM delta mappings requiring schema changes for onboarding flows.
Tier 2 (Medium, SLA 5d): Role template additions, non-blocking SSO attribute mapping requests, small SCIM group adjustments.
Tier 3 (Low, Backlog): Optimization requests, cosmetic role naming, policy wishlist items without immediate customer impact.

Automated scorer inputs (data sources):
- Customer tier (from billing/CRM)
- Number of impacted users (support ticket metadata)
- Revenue at risk (from sales metadata)
- Security tag (SAML/SCIM auth failure, HIPAA/ISO-sensitivity flag)
- Complexity estimate (detected: requires infra change, requires config-only)
- Requested due date and legal/contract constraint

Decision rules & routing:
- Score >= 80 -> escalate to on-call enterprise solutions + Eng triage (Tier 0/1)
- Score 50-79 -> PM review -> Solutions engineering assignment (Tier 1/2)
- Score < 50 -> Product backlog or self-serve guidance (Tier 3)
- For requests flagged 'security_tag' or 'regulatory', always require 'security_review_required' and immediate notification to Security Ops.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public triage rubric documented in Confluence with examples (SAML failure, RBAC request, SCIM diff)
- Prototype scorer implemented as a lightweight webhook in Intake service that returns {priority_score, tier, route_destination} (mocked for the pilot)
- Routing paths configured: support -> intake webhook -> PM queue / Solutions queue / Eng on-call
- SLA tracker dashboard in Console (new per-request SLA metric) showing triage-to-ack and triage-to-resolution by tier
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers (one regulated, one SaaS-scale, one mid-market) and feedback captured

Trade-offs / Notes:
- Heuristic aggressiveness: stricter scoring reduces time-to-ack for critical customers but increases operational load; keep pilot small and measure load before global rollout.
- SCIM schema complexity: some customers require custom attribute transforms; these should be captured as "complexity: high" and routed to Eng.
- RBAC policy proliferation risk: encourage reuse patterns and introduce a "role-template registry" to avoid bespoke roles.

Artifacts / Links:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/PM-95432+Priority+Ladder+PRD
- Intake webhook PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/intake-priority-poc (PR #23)
- Design notes for consent flows and admin UX: Google Drive > Design/Admin-Onboard-Pilot-v2

Review feedback (summary):
- Security: require mandatory KBA for SAML cert rotations; include audit-log sample for each routed request. (Action: add audit artifact requirement)
- Solutions: want a "fast reject" path when insufficient artifacts provided (SAML metadata missing) with templated customer responses. (Action: add pre-checker)
- Eng: wary of automations that create noise in on-call; prefer canary enablement per customer. (Action: add canary toggle in Intake service)

Metrics to measure (pilot):
- Mean time triage -> first ack (goal: Tier0 <4h, Tier1 <24h)
- % requests correctly classified (manual audit sample)
- On-call interrupt rate increase (alerts/day) during pilot
- Customer satisfaction NPS for onboarding (pre/post pilot)

Rollout plan:
1) Week 0-2: finalize rubric, Confluence PRD, implement webhook PoC and pre-checker
2) Week 3: pilot with 3 customers, enable canary toggles per org
3) Week 4-6: gather metrics, iterate heuristics, add role-template registry for RBAC reuse
4) Week 7: propose company-wide rollout and include in Console routing UI
